title: Generate Parentheses
statement: Given a number n, list every well-formed string made of exactly n pairs of round brackets. Well-formed means each closing bracket matches an earlier opening one. The strings may come back in any order.

example.caption: Two pairs give two strings: nested, or side by side.

idea.sentence: Build the string one character at a time, adding a bracket only when it keeps the string valid, and undo the choice to try the other.

jargon.plain: Try a choice, explore everything that follows, then undo it and try the next choice.
A function that calls itself for the smaller problem that is left.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the number of pairs n, e.g. 3 (keep it small)

compare.bruteLabel: Try all 2^(2n) strings, then check each

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: Make every string of 2n brackets and check each one. Most are invalid.

rows.name: Backtracking
rows.note: Roughly the count of valid strings (the Catalan number) times n to build each. Dead ends are never entered. Space is the recursion depth, not counting the output.

fast.takeaway: Both are exponential, since the answer itself is huge. Backtracking never wastes time on strings that were already broken.

stages.title: Start empty
stages.note: path is the string built so far. It works like a stack: push a bracket, recurse, pop it.

stages.title: Open if allowed
stages.note: Add "(" while fewer than n have been opened.

stages.title: Close if allowed
stages.note: Add ")" only when more are open than closed. That keeps every prefix valid.

stages.title: Complete
stages.note: When the string has 2n characters it is valid by construction. Save a copy.

stages.title: Undo and return
stages.note: Pop the bracket after exploring it so the other choice starts from the same string. Return all results.

edges.title: One pair
edges.why: Only one choice at each step: open, then close.

edges.title: Two pairs
edges.why: After the first "(" you may open again or close. Both branches are real.

edges.title: Count grows fast
edges.why: The count is the Catalan number. The output itself is large, so no solution can be fast.

edges.title: Never close first
edges.why: close < open is false when both are 0, so ")" cannot start a string.

gotchas.text: Push path.join("") into the result, not path. Pushing the array stores a reference that later pops will empty.
Save string(path), which copies the bytes. Appending path itself would alias one shared backing array, and every saved result would change as the search continues.
Do not name a variable close. It hides the built-in close function and go vet may warn. The code uses opened and closed.
Check close < open, not close < n. With close < n you build strings like "())(" that are invalid.
Pop after the recursive call, in both branches. Forgetting one leaves stray characters in the next branch.
The result order is up to you. Compare as a set, as the tests do.

recap.key: Open while opens < n. Close while closes < opens. Record at length 2n. Pop after each try.
recap.complexity: Time about O(4ⁿ / √n). Space O(n) for the recursion.
moves: Track how many are opened and closed
At 2n characters save a copy, then pop to backtrack
